title: Affine atlas relation towers and mixed products over a quasi-separated space
statement:
Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. An affine scheme is a spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every affine scheme has quasi-compact source; quasi-separated means that its diagonal is quasi-compact. A space is quasi-separated when its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source over every affine scheme test. Let $Y$ be a quasi-separated algebraic space, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, $(Z_a\to Y)_{a\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transitions, and $Z=\varprojlim_aZ_a$ a limit in algebraic spaces over $Y$. Fix $o\in I$ and a representable surjective etale atlas $U_o\to Z_o$ with $U_o$ affine. For $a\ge o$ put $U_a=U_o\times_{Z_o}Z_a$, $U=U_o\times_{Z_o}Z$, $R_a=U_a\times_{Z_a}U_a$, and $R=U\times_ZU$, with projections $s_a,t_a$ and $s,t$ to the first and second factors. Then $U_a$ and $U$ are affine schemes, their maps to $Z_a,Z$ are representable surjective etale, and $U=\varprojlim_{a\ge o}U_a$ as schemes, with affine transitions. The objects $R_a,R$ are quasi-compact separated schemes; their two projections are etale and of finite type, and the maps $j_a=(s_a,t_a):R_a\to U_a\times_YU_a$ are locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every $a,b\ge o$, the sheaf product $U_a\times_YU_b$ is a quasi-compact separated scheme. More generally, for every affine scheme $W$ with a map $W\to Y$ and every $a\ge o$, the schemes $V_b=W\times_YU_b$ ($b\ge a$) are quasi-compact and separated, have affine transition maps, and have limit $V=W\times_YU$ as schemes. For $b\ge a$, the map $h_{a,b}:R_b\to U_a\times_YU_b$, $r\mapsto(u_{ba}s_b(r),t_b(r))$, where $u_{ba}:U_b\to U_a$ is the transition, is the base change of $j_a$ along $1\times u_{ba}$. More precisely there are canonical isomorphisms, preserving the displayed maps,
$$R_b\cong R_a\times_{t_a,U_a}U_b\cong R_a\times_{U_a\times_YU_a}(U_a\times_YU_b),\qquad R\cong R_a\times_{t_a,U_a}U.$$
No separatedness of $Z_a\to Y$ or $Z\to Y$, finite presentation of a stage over $Y$, or quasi-compactness of $Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: Restrict to the upper tail $I_{\ge o}$. It is directed: a common upper bound of two elements remains above $o$. A cone on the tail extends uniquely to $I$: its component at $i$ is obtained through any common upper bound of $i,o$, independently of that choice by passing to a further upper bound. Thus the given limit is unchanged. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], each $Z\to Z_a$ is affine, and $U\cong\varprojlim_{a\ge o}U_a$ as spaces. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], base change of the affine maps $Z_b\to Z_a$ makes $U_b\to U_a$ affine, and $U_a\to U_o$ and $U\to U_o$ affine. Their target is affine, so all $U_a,U$ are affine schemes. The space limit universal property restricts to scheme tests, giving the stated scheme limit.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: Each $U_a\to Z_a$ is the pullback of $U_o\to Z_o$, as is $U\to Z$. Apply [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to the singleton surjective etale covering. These maps remain representable, surjective and etale. Their self-fibre-products $R_a$ and $R$ are schemes: they are base changes of these representable maps to the schemes $U_a,U$. Both projections of each relation are etale, by the same pullback assertion.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: For any two affine schemes $A,B\to Y$, their product over $Y$ is a scheme: the representable diagonal of $Y$ represents $A\times_YB$ over $A\times_{\mathbf Z}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the latter is affine. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-product-comparison] to $A,B\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: the comparison $A\times_YB\to A\times_{\mathbf Z}B$ is separated. Then [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] shows that $A\times_YB$ is separated. Finally [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated] gives its quasi-compactness directly from the affine-test criterion for $Y$. Taking $(A,B)=(U_a,U_b)$ or $(W,U_b)$ proves every asserted finite-stage mixed-product finiteness statement.

Apply the same comparison lemma to $U_a,U_a\to Z_a\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. It makes $R_a$ separated over the affine scheme $U_a\times_{\mathbf Z}U_a$, hence absolutely separated by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated]. Since $Z_a$ is quasi-separated, [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated] makes $R_a$ quasi-compact. For $j_a$, instead apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-product-comparison] to $U_a,U_a\to Z_a\to Y$; its locally finite type assertion is exactly the assertion about $j_a$. This uses no separatedness of $Z_a\to Y$.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: Write $p_a:U_a\to Z_a$. For a scheme test $T$, a section of $R_a\times_{t_a,U_a}U_b$ is $(x,y,v)$ with $p_a(x)=p_a(y)$ and $y=u_{ba}(v)$. Write $v=(v_o,z_b)$ under $U_b=U_o\times_{Z_o}Z_b$. If $x=(x_o,z_a)$, the equality forces $z_a$ to be the image of $z_b$. Therefore $x_b=(x_o,z_b)$ is a well-defined section of $U_b$ and $(x_b,v)\in R_b(T)$. This is inverse to $(x_b,v)\mapsto(u_{ba}(x_b),u_{ba}(v),v)$. The formulas are natural in $T$, so they give the first canonical isomorphism. The identical formulas with $Z,U$ in place of $Z_b,U_b$ give $R\cong R_a\times_{t_a,U_a}U$.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: A test section of $R_a\times_{U_a\times_YU_a}(U_a\times_YU_b)$ is $(r,x,v)$ subject to $s_a(r)=x$ and $t_a(r)=u_{ba}(v)$. Forgetting $x$ gives $R_a\times_{t_a,U_a}U_b$, with inverse $(r,v)\mapsto(r,s_a(r),v)$. Under step 5 its projection to $U_a\times_YU_b$ is $(u_{ba}s_b,t_b)=h_{a,b}$. Hence the required square is cartesian along $1\times u_{ba}$, with the displayed order of the projections preserved.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: Fix any $a\ge o$. Step 1 makes $U\to U_a$ affine; by step 5, $R\to R_a$ is its base change along $t_a$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] it is affine and quasi-compact, so its pullback over the quasi-compact scheme $R_a$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. This pullback is $R$ itself. For separatedness apply [lem-sfb-space-fibre-product-comparison] to $U,U\to Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: it gives a separated morphism $R\to U\times_{\mathbf Z}U$. The target is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], hence [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] makes $R$ absolutely separated. This avoids any assumption that $Z$ is separated or any separate assertion of quasi-separatedness of the limit.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: For $s_a,t_a:R_a\to U_a$ and $s,t:R\to U$, the source is quasi-compact by steps 4 and 7, and the target is affine, hence quasi-separated: for affine schemes $A,B$ over an affine target $\operatorname{Spec}C$, the product $A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}B$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], hence quasi-compact, which is the affine-test criterion of [def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated]. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] each projection is quasi-compact. They are etale by step 2 and therefore locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A finitely presented algebra $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ is generated by the $n$ displayed classes [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so each projection is locally of finite type. The definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] now gives finite type.

source.place: Tag 084T (lemma-descend-separated), atlas and mixed-product construction; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: For $b\ge c\ge a$, $W\times_YU_b\cong(W\times_YU_c)\times_{U_c}U_b$, so the transitions $V_b\to V_c$ are affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. A compatible family of maps from a scheme $T$ to $V_b$ consists of one map $w:T\to W$ and a compatible family $v_b:T\to U_b$ with equal images in $Y$. Step 1 gives a unique $v:T\to U$. The two maps $T\to Y$ agree because their common value is already the image of $v_a$; hence $(w,v)$ defines a unique map to $W\times_YU$. This proves the scheme limit property, since step 3 also applies to $A=W,B=U$ and shows that $V$ is a scheme. All indexing tails remain small and nonempty.
